title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput benchmark results on staging, iterate continuous batching and concurrency targets. Key takeaways: 1) current config (max_batch=128, batch_timeout=12ms, concurrency=8 per GPU) hits target p95 latency for 90% of traffic but has queue spikes during bursts; 2) Samir to run a 2x concurrency + smaller max_batch run to validate tail latency; 3) enable prefix KV caching for routable requests and test reduced batch timeout for low-latency slices. Next steps: new benchmark by 2026-09-04, cost estimate update, and a short follow-up demo of queueing dashboard.
action_items: Samir Patel: Run 2x concurrency run on staging with max_batch=64 and batch_timeout=8ms; output csv to shared benchmark sheet (due 2026-09-04)
Carlos Rivera: Provide 24hr production-like request trace for burst pattern analysis (due 2026-09-03)
Maya Chen: Send updated pricing delta estimate for 2x concurrency scenario and Redis KV caching notes (due 2026-09-05)
Daniel Kim: Validate prefix caching coverage on sample traffic and flag edge cases (due 2026-09-06)
next_steps: SE-run benchmark with 2x concurrency + smaller batch sizes
Customer to share request trace for realistic burst emulation
Redwood to update cost delta and autoscaling recommendation
Schedule a 30m follow-up to review new results (proposed 2026-09-07)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Carlos Rivera: Carlos here, hi.
[00:07] Leah Park: Leah here.
[00:09] Daniel Kim: Daniel on the line.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Great, Samir is with me from the SE team.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Hey all. Alright, agenda — look at the latest throughput runs, talk through continuous batching tweaks, and confirm next runs.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Quick reminder the shared benchmark sheet is in the deck link I posted in the calendar invite, it's the - Benchmark_Sept.csv - please look.
[00:35] Carlos Rivera: Yep saw it, thanks. So initial question: the p95 we're seeing in staging is 220ms but in spikes it goes to 420ms. Is that from batching?
[00:47] Samir Patel: So from our end the main contributor was queue delay — when concurrency is small we get larger per-request queuing while we fill batches. With max_batch 128 and batch_timeout 12ms you see good throughput but tail suffers if you get bursty arrival patterns.
[01:05] Daniel Kim: Right, that matches what we saw. During payment peak windows we get big microbursts.
[01:13] Samir Patel: Two knobs: lower batch_timeout (to reduce waiting to fill batch) and lower max_batch, or increase concurrency to process more batches in parallel. Each has cost/latency tradeoffs.
[01:25] Leah Park: Can you remind us of the latency SLO again? p95 under 250ms ideally, p99 under 600ms.
[01:30] Maya Chen: Correct — those are the success criteria we agreed.
[01:33] Samir Patel: Ok, looking at run #7 in the sheet — that was concurrency=8 per GPU, max_batch=128, batch_timeout=12ms. Average tokens/sec was ~14k, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~540ms. The p99 spikes aligned with >3x arrival bursts.
[01:50] Carlos Rivera: The cost looked ok but doubling concurrency might double instance usage, right?
[01:55] Samir Patel: Not necessarily double instance count, but it will raise GPU utilization and affect cost per token. We need to run the 2x concurrency to measure marginal cost. Also autoscaling rules can help — keep baseline concurrency lower and spin up additional nodes during sustained bursts.
[02:12] Daniel Kim: Is KV cache helping here? We have a lot of repeated prefixes in auth flows.
[02:15] Samir Patel: Yes prefix/KV caching reduces compute by cutting off early for previously seen prefixes. For inference it's a big win on repeat flows. We saw 18-23% token reduction when enabled in earlier tests, which directly improves throughput and lowers cost. But caching doesn't help cold-start user prompts.
[02:35] Leah Park: Any gotchas with the caching we should know?
[02:38] Samir Patel: Watch cache miss amplification if the cache is too small, and ensure your routing policy respects staleness if you run multiple model variants. Also, encryption/KMS doesn't impact caching logic but is important for private deployments.
[02:52] Maya Chen: Carlos, did you get a chance to export a real traffic trace? That will help us simulate microburst patterns.
[02:58] Carlos Rivera: I'm working with infra, we can probably get a 24hr trace by tomorrow.
[03:02] Samir Patel: Great — with that we'll run the reproduced trace through our staging harness and do a sensitivity sweep: concurrency 8 -> 16, max_batch 128 -> 64, batch_timeout 12ms -> 8ms and 5ms.
[03:15] Daniel Kim: Any concerns about model quality with higher concurrency?
[03:18] Samir Patel: Concurrency itself doesn't change quality, but if we route to quantized variants to save cost then there may be small quality deltas. We'll keep the same model weights for these runs.
[03:29] Maya Chen: We also talked about queueing dashboard — Samir you demoed it last week, can we add the latency breakdown by queue wait time vs inference time?
[03:36] Samir Patel: Yep can add a per-route breakdown and p95 of queue wait. It's in the console's per-route panel. I'll add a quick demo screenshot to the sheet.
[03:44] Leah Park: For the autoscaling policy, what's your recommended threshold?
[03:47] Samir Patel: We usually trigger scale-up when queue length > N (depends on model and SLO). For you, preliminary recommendation: trigger if p95 queue wait > 40ms sustained for 60s, scale by one node. We'll validate with the trace.
[04:00] Carlos Rivera: Sounds reasonable. Also curious about cost math — Maya will send estimate?
[04:04] Maya Chen: Yes I'll update the cost delta for the 2x concurrency scenario and include both per-hour and per-10k-token cost lines.
[04:12] Daniel Kim: One more — does the platform support request-level prioritization? We want payments to have priority over analytics queries.
[04:18] Samir Patel: Yes, request routing policies can set priority weights and we can reserve capacity for high-priority routes. We can demo that in the follow-up.
[04:26] Leah Park: Great. Any blockers from the Redwood side?
[04:29] Samir Patel: None. We'll need Carlos's trace and we'll run the sensitivity matrix and share raw logs and aggregated metrics.
[04:36] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap action items — Samir will run the 2x concurrency + smaller batch runs and upload csv; Carlos to share trace; Maya to send cost delta and notes; Daniel to check prefix caching edge cases.
[04:49] Carlos Rivera: Got it.
[04:50] Leah Park: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[04:53] Maya Chen: Thanks — I'll propose a 30m follow-up on 2026-09-07, 10am PT.
[04:57] Daniel Kim: Works for me.
[04:58] Samir Patel: Thanks all.
[05:00] [call ends]
